title: PowerPoint on the web: Copilot Agent Mode creates presentations from Work IQ
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licence-assignment path and PowerShell command are supported. It correctly identifies the release-notes instructions as Windows-only and distinguishes included Work IQ access from separately billed API usage; web-specific defaults and entitlement details remain unconfirmed.

claims.claim: Work IQ is a workplace intelligence layer that enables agents to access and reason over organizational and business data.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The Work IQ presentation release-notes entry is explicitly marked Windows.
claims.quote: Create presentations with Work IQ using Agent Mode in Copilot in PowerPoint [Windows]

claims.claim: The release notes say Copilot uses Work IQ to automatically gather relevant files, meetings and emails for presentations.
claims.quote: Copilot in PowerPoint now uses Work IQ to automatically gather relevant files, meetings, and emails to help build presentations.

claims.claim: The Windows release-notes instructions start by opening PowerPoint and selecting Edit with Copilot.
claims.quote: Open PowerPoint and select 'Edit with Copilot'.

claims.claim: The Windows release-notes instructions then say to choose to create a presentation based on Work IQ.
claims.quote: Choose to create a presentation based on your Work IQ.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn page specifically documenting this Work IQ capability on the web was found at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: 'PowerPoint Work IQ web 555873'; 'Agent Mode in PowerPoint web'. Read release notes, Work IQ overview and Copilot overview; results covered Windows, generic web PowerPoint or separate API tools, not this web capability.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The default and any required administrator enablement for this web feature are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: 'PowerPoint Work IQ admin default'; 'Create presentations with Work IQ PowerPoint default admin'. Read roadmap, release notes, Work IQ overview and Copilot overview; no web-feature default or required admin action found.

claims.claim: The supplied roadmap record gives no rollout mechanics.
claims.quote: Searched: read the complete roadmap record for rollout channel, deployment sequence and tenant rollout mechanics; it lists status, target, release phase, cloud and platform but no mechanics.

claims.claim: The supplied roadmap record gives no prerequisites.
claims.quote: Searched: read the complete roadmap record for prerequisites, licence requirements and enablement requirements; none are provided.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft describes Work IQ actions as user scoped, with each request running in a specific user's context.
claims.quote: Actions are user scoped, meaning every request runs in the context of a specific user

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Work IQ accesses only what that user is allowed to see or do.
claims.quote: Actions are user scoped, meaning every request runs in the context of a specific user and only accesses what that user is allowed to see or do.

claims.claim: The roadmap item does not say where the generated presentation is saved.
claims.quote: Searched: read the entire roadmap record for save location or output storage; the description addresses presentation creation and finding source content only.

claims.claim: The roadmap item does not specify sensitivity-label inheritance from source content.
claims.quote: Searched: read the entire roadmap record for sensitivity labels, inheritance and source-label handling; none are mentioned.

claims.claim: Neither the roadmap item nor the relevant release-notes entry describes a separate identity for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: read the roadmap description and July 01, 2026 Work IQ presentation entry in Copilot release notes for a separate agent or service identity; neither describes one.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not describe sending the presentation.
claims.quote: Searched: read the roadmap record for sending or distribution actions; it describes creating presentations and finding files, meetings and emails only.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not describe sharing the presentation.
claims.quote: Searched: read the roadmap record for sharing, publishing or permission changes; it describes creating presentations and finding source content only.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The Copilot overview describes a Basic experience with in-app PowerPoint access for users without the Copilot add-on licence.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) refers to users without the Copilot add-on license, but who have access to Copilot capabilities inside apps (for example, Word or Excel).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Copilot overview ties the full PowerPoint Copilot experience to the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: The Basic experience is subject to fair use limits.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) refers to users without the Copilot add-on license, but who have access to Copilot capabilities inside apps (for example, Word or Excel). It doesn't include full chat integration. Some features are subject to fair use limits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: For Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users, Work IQ is available in all Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences and agents.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users, Work IQ is available in all Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences and agents.

claims.claim: The Work IQ page says usage-based billing applies to custom and third-party agents.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users, Work IQ is available in all Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences and agents. It is subject to usage-based billing for custom and third-party agents.

claims.claim: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing.
claims.quote: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.

claims.claim: The roadmap item names no meter or price for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: read the complete roadmap record for price, billing, meter, credits and consumption; none are specified.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A licence or credit rule specific to this Work IQ option in PowerPoint Agent Mode was not found at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Create presentations with Work IQ PowerPoint license'; 'Agent Mode PowerPoint Work IQ licensing Basic Premium'. Read Copilot overview, license options, Work IQ overview and release notes; only product-level entitlement and separate API billing found.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: Whether Basic-experience users can use the web Work IQ presentation option is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: 'PowerPoint Work IQ Agent Mode license web'; 'Agent Mode PowerPoint Work IQ licensing Basic Premium'. Read Copilot overview, license options, Work IQ overview and release notes; no entitlement for Basic users to this web option found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is included because Work IQ comes with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium), unlike the distinct Work IQ API offering.
claims.quote: Although both use the Work IQ platform, Work IQ is included with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium), whereas the Work IQ API is a distinct usage-based billing offering

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least the License Administrator or User Administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: User licence assignment is under Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a licence to the identified user.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()
